summary: Bound ordinary forwarded client reads and stop their timed-out relay futures.

replay.detail: No replay, heal or projection-health behavior change. Heal-next is a mutating protocol step; its reported 49.3 s duration is not improved by this change.

schema.detail: No table, index, schema version or claim vocabulary change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule or authority change.

compatibility.detail: Forwarded read envelopes use 15 s including body, queue, relay and response work, plus the supported operation long-poll wait (capped at 10 s), instead of the 120 s bulk budget. Each query keeps its separate 15 s child budget. Only the forwarding route newly drops its handler-owned relay future on timeout; other GET/HEAD handlers retain existing cooperative cancellation. Body timeouts log bounded route, phase and callsite. Terminal actions keep mutation acknowledgement semantics. Public 30 s long-poll and 120 s bulk/doctor budgets remain. A relay may return a generic 504/read-deadline before the owner-specific response because its local envelope does not add the HTTP client hop margin. Read-deadline ends route selection without trying an alternate hop; old gateways may map it to 503/remote-unavailable. Synchronous CPU/SQLite/IO granules still require cooperative checks; async timeouts do not preempt them.

downtime.detail: Normal daemon rollout required; restart and mixed-version behavior not independently qualified.

manual.detail: No settings or data repair required.

recovery.detail: Rollback restores the previous forwarding budget; no data migration.
